findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/owner-session-token-store.ts:41-65,119-132 and packages/main/src/handlers/doctor.ts:279-286,490-494 — HIGH: generated-token storage has no lifecycle cleanup or doctor inspection/repair, despite the ratified contract R3 requiring storage ownership, cleanup, and doctor visibility. The writer publishes directly to the final path with flag wx; a partial/corrupt final file is treated as unreadable, then every retry gets EEXIST and rethrows forever. Repro on current dist: create one token, replace its JSON with {partial, then call readOrCreateOwnerSessionToken for the same dimensions => ERROR_CODE=EEXIST. This can permanently brick a supported generated-token boundary until an undocumented manual deletion, and tokens otherwise accumulate without expiry/owner-scoped cleanup.

packages/main/src/core/lattice-dispatch.ts:1682-1687 — HIGH: buildCanonicalHostRuntimeEnv re-adds process.env.LATTICE_SESSION_ID whenever envAllowlist contains it, without honoring envDenylist. This bypasses buildRequiredCommandEnv deny precedence and can propagate the parent owner identity into a reviewer child even under an explicit deny policy, collapsing role isolation. Repro on current dist with both lists containing LATTICE_SESSION_ID returns DENYLIST_RESULT=must-stay-denied instead of absent. Preserve explicit override only when allowlisted AND not denied, with a regression for conflicting policy entries.

packages/main/src/core/owner-session-adapters.ts:26-31,63-68 and 130-138 never consume the real Codex task signal CODEX_THREAD_ID and there is no direct Codex wrapper/adapter injection path for LATTICE_OWNER_SESSION_ADAPTER_TASK plus AGENT. In this live Codex task, the environment has CODEX_THREAD_ID but none of CODEX_SESSION_ID/OPENAI_SESSION_ID/TERM_SESSION_ID/LATTICE_AGENT; `env -u LATTICE_SESSION_ID node bin/lattice.js session_brief` therefore reports `[derived-ppid]`. WHY: the shipped path still requires the same manual LATTICE_SESSION_ID workaround and does not solve cross-shell self-lock for the ordinary Codex owner task, despite CHK-001/002 claiming supported adapter stability. Add a validated direct-host bridge that maps the actual durable Codex task signal plus a policy-distinct main/agent role into the canonical composite, with child-shell propagation and a real CLI regression proving two PPIDs keep one id while another task/role differs.

docs/requirements/decisions/owner-session-contract-execution-plan.md:397-404 and 445-461 require a post-implementation R5 run on at least two real hosts and explicitly state that pre-implementation document reviews do not satisfy it. CHK-002 currently binds every supported-host intent only to deterministic logic/smoke tests on a175883c, while the two real-host records in CHK-004 are pre-runtime document reviews. WHY: the story cannot yet claim that the implemented Codex/Claude/agy bridges work in their real launch environments, and the missing real-host run is exactly where the live Codex-variable mismatch escaped. Run the final implementation on two independent real providers (including the actual direct owner-task path), bind exact post-implementation HEAD/material/storyFiles hashes, and keep degraded ppid as the required negative control.

packages/main/src/tasks/story-owner-lease-smoke.ts:102-440 — HIGH coverage gap: CHK-002 binds every must intent to a same-process resolver/env-builder smoke, but the required cross-process contract is not exercised. The test directly calls resolveSessionIdentity/buildCanonicalHostRuntimeEnv and intercepts console.warn; it never spawns the required nested child shells, never invokes session_brief or doctor through the CLI, and never scans child stdout/stderr/activity/evidence for provider sentinels. packages/main/src/tasks/cli-surface-smoke.ts contains no owner-session assertions and is unchanged in this story despite being cited by the evidence. packages/main/src/core/owner-session-token-store.ts:120-130 also adds wx/EEXIST race recovery without a concurrent-writer regression. WHY: the shipped failure occurs across shell/process boundaries, so same-process helper PASS can miss lost child env, cache/reset, CLI rendering, warning-before-write, disclosure, and two-writer token divergence. Add bounded focused regressions that (1) spawn nested provider child processes for Codex/Claude/agy/fake identities and assert stable task/role isolation plus exact session_brief/doctor/pre-mutation diagnostics and redaction, (2) exercise blank explicit override and deliberate allowlisted override through the spawned boundary, (3) race two generated-token creators for one scope and prove one stable token with scoped separation, and (4) retain existing takeover/lifecycle consumer checks. Rebind only the intents actually asserted.

docs/requirements/decisions/owner-session-contract-execution-plan.md:397-404 and CHK-002 verificationEvidence — HIGH: the ratified contract requires a post-implementation matrix on at least two real hosts and explicitly says pre-implementation document reviews do not count, while every CHK-002 real-host/child-shell intent is marked satisfied only by deterministic story-owner-lease/guardrail/CLI smokes. Those tests exercise synthetic env objects, not actual Codex/Claude/Antigravity launcher propagation or nested child shells, so host-specific env loss and source/provider drift remain untested. Run and bind fresh post-implementation real-host transcripts (at least two providers, plus one degraded ppid negative) or keep the affected intents/checklist incomplete.
